summary: Capture completed Claude response usage on native transcript writes

replay.detail: No claim replay or historical aggregate rewrite is required.

schema.detail: No database, claim, registry or client schema changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, fleet or authorization rules change.

compatibility.detail: Native st3 Claude wrappers and adopted wrappers watch their exact session-bound main and subagent transcripts with shallow filesystem subscriptions. Completed responses are captured during long turns and after Stop returns. An independent durable cursor preserves native user-turn lineage across writes and ignores partial or unfinished streaming records. Stop hooks retain their answer and usage publication; response source IDs retain existing deduplication. Accounting observation failures do not gate provider launch or adoption: existing Stop-time acquisition continues independently, while st doctor warns that native write observation is unavailable. Backend errors rescan the bound files without terminating observation. Session-specific event filtering and a single queued wake coalesce streaming writes; subscriptions retire old session paths and re-register replaced directory inodes. The shared Stop/subagent normalizer also rejects explicitly unfinished stop_reason:null usage, so Stop cannot reserve a response ID with provisional counters before the observer sees completion; legacy native records without that field keep their existing behavior.

downtime.detail: Normal driver binary adoption starts the observer without restarting the Claude process or its native session.

manual.detail: The first observer cursor starts at the existing exact-session Stop cursor and scans its prefix only to recover turn lineage. Previously consumed history is not replayed or repriced. Retain measured snapshots; old retired-session final replies remain explicit acquisition gaps, and choose a new clean measurement window after verified installation. If doctor reports malformed, truncated or invalid-cursor acquisition, preserve the transcript, all usage cursors and the observation status first. Repair the named watch limit, permissions or native-store fault. Restore a damaged cursor only from an audited same-session backup and reconcile source IDs; never delete it to replay history. Re-adopt the wrapper through the normal binary path after repair. If the original lineage cannot be recovered, keep the affected measurement inconclusive and begin a fresh verified window; do not invent or reprice missing usage. Repeated identical errors log once per unresolved episode; repeat counts are accumulated and published on a new cause or shutdown, and included on recovery. A notify error followed by an idle period remains unavailable in doctor until a later successful real change or a final drain; a rescan alone does not assert watch recovery. During a daemon rollout, wrappers on older binaries have no current-incarnation observation status and will warn until normal binary adoption installs the observer; this is acquisition-unavailable evidence, not proof that native agent supervision failed. Interrupted responses that never finalize are not priced. Their native provisional usage remains an explicit acquisition gap in cost coverage and before/after audits; retain those rows in the native inventory and do not claim complete cost coverage while they are unaccounted for.

recovery.detail: Binary rollback removes the transcript observer and restores Stop-only acquisition; recorded usage and the separate cursor remain durable. No threshold, access, mailbox, queue or native-session change.
